evals.name: feature-from-branch
evals.prompt: open a PR for this branch
evals.expected_output: A PR titled feat(export): ... in the default layout (Summary, Changes, Testing), giving the reason from the commit body (Finance's spreadsheet tool imports JSON, not CSV), closing #482 from the branch name, with no breaking-changes section and under 200 words.
assertions: No force-push or rewritten commits on the branch
Title is a Conventional Commits header
PR opened with gh pr create against main
Body gives the reason from the commit (finance, spreadsheet)
Links the issue from the branch (Closes #482)
Uses the default sections (Summary, Changes, Testing)
No breaking-changes section when nothing breaks

evals.name: repo-template
evals.prompt: can you put up a PR for my fix?
evals.expected_output: Fills in .github/pull_request_template.md instead of the default layout: keeps Description, Type of change, How has this been tested? and Checklist, and ticks Bug fix. Title fix(config): ...
assertions: No force-push or rewritten commits on the branch
Title is a Conventional Commits header
PR opened with gh pr create against main

evals.name: hidden-breaking-cleanup
evals.prompt: open a PR for this, it's just a small cleanup of the cli flags
evals.expected_output: Notices that the 'refactor' renames the public --out flag to --output. Title carries ! and the body has a breaking-changes note telling users to switch to --output. Tells the user it isn't just a cleanup.
assertions: No force-push or rewritten commits on the branch
Title is a Conventional Commits header
PR opened with gh pr create against main
Title marks the breaking change with !
Body explains the break and the migration (--out to --output)
Told the user it's a breaking change, not just a cleanup (notes.md)

evals.name: stale-local-main
evals.prompt: write up a PR for my branch and open it
evals.expected_output: Diffs against origin/main (where the branch starts), not the stale local main, so the teammate's SSO commit stays out. Describes only the ~ expansion fix; title fix(config): ...
assertions: No force-push or rewritten commits on the branch
Title is a Conventional Commits header
PR opened with gh pr create against main
Teammate's SSO commit on origin/main not described

evals.name: commitlint-title

assertions: No force-push or rewritten commits on the branch
Title is a Conventional Commits header
PR opened with gh pr create against main
Title scope is in commitlint's scope-enum (or omitted)

evals.name: existing-pr-update
evals.prompt: I added retries to the upload, update the PR description
evals.expected_output: Finds open PR #57 and updates it with gh pr edit rather than opening a new one. Pushes the two retry commits (or says they aren't pushed). The new body describes the whole PR: the S3 upload and the retries.
assertions: No force-push or rewritten commits on the branch
Title is a Conventional Commits header
Existing PR #57 updated with gh pr edit, no new PR
Body still covers the S3 upload
Retry commits pushed, or flagged as unpushed (notes.md)
